users.title: Users
users.description: Who can sign in and which projects each person reaches.
users.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the current one.
users.deleteDescription: {{email}} loses access at once, and their API keys stop working.
users.deactivateDescription: {{email}} is signed out at once and can't sign in until someone brings the account back. Their API keys are revoked for good.
users.accessHint: Viewers see states and inventory. Operators can also configure and deploy.
users.hostAdminHint: Open a shell on the server, read its disk and reboot it. A service's console stays with administrators.
users.hostAdminOwnerOnly: Only the owner can change this.
users.changeOwnAccount: Change your own on your Authentication page.
users.roleHint: What this account can reach on this server.

keys.title: API keys
keys.description: Keys act with your rights, limited to the projects and level you choose. Each one is shown once.
keys.name: Name
keys.expiresHint: Days until it stops working, {{max}} at most.
keys.scopeHint: Leave all unchecked for every project you reach.
keys.scopeHintAdmin: Leave all unchecked for every project.
keys.revokeDescription: Anything using {{name}} stops working at once.
keys.shownOnce: Copy it now. It won't be shown again.
keys.emptyDescription: Create one to use the API from a script or a CI job.
keys.nameHint: A name to tell this key apart.
keys.secretHint: Copy it now. It isn't shown again.

invitations.title: Invite people
invitations.description: Each person gets a link to choose their own password. It works once and expires after {{days}} days.
invitations.emailsHint: One per line, or separated by commas or spaces. At most {{max}} at a time.
invitations.roleHint: Everyone in this list gets the same rights. You can change each account once it exists.
invitations.byLink: Show me the links to pass on
invitations.byEmailHint: Each person receives their own link. The list of invitations shows when it has gone.
invitations.byLinkHint: The links show once, here, for you to pass on yourself.
invitations.noChannel: No email channel is set up, so the links will show here for you to pass on.
invitations.addChannel: Add an SMTP channel in Notifications
invitations.linksWarning: Copy these links now: they won't be shown again. Each works once, until it expires.
invitations.linkWarning: Copy this link now: it won't be shown again. The previous one no longer works.
invitations.emailsQueued: The emails are on their way. The list of invitations shows when each one has gone.
invitations.pendingDescription: People invited who haven't created their account yet.
invitations.resendDescription: {{email}} gets a new link, valid for {{days}} days. The previous one stops working.
invitations.revokeDescription: The link sent to {{email}} stops working at once.

errors.none: Enter at least one email address.
errors.tooMany: At most {{max}} addresses at a time.

twoFactorPolicy.require: Require two-factor sign-in for every account
twoFactorPolicy.hint_one: An account without it can then only turn it on, and its API keys stop working until it does. {{count}} account doesn't use it yet.
twoFactorPolicy.hint_other: An account without it can then only turn it on, and its API keys stop working until it does. {{count}} accounts don't use it yet.
twoFactorPolicy.hint_zero: An account without it can then only turn it on, and its API keys stop working until it does. Every active account already uses it.
twoFactorPolicy.requiredHint_one: Required. {{count}} account still has to turn it on.
twoFactorPolicy.requiredHint_other: Required. {{count}} accounts still have to turn it on.
twoFactorPolicy.requiredHint_zero: Required. Every active account uses it.
twoFactorPolicy.ownerOnly: Only the owner can change this.
twoFactorPolicy.ownFirst: Turn on two-factor sign-in on your own account first, on your Authentication page.
twoFactorPolicy.confirmDescription_one: {{count}} account doesn't use it yet: until it turns it on, that is all it will be able to do.
twoFactorPolicy.confirmDescription_other: {{count}} accounts don't use it yet: until they turn it on, that is all they will be able to do.
twoFactorPolicy.confirmDescription_zero: Every active account already uses it. A new account will have to turn it on before it can do anything else.
twoFactorPolicy.notRequiredDone: Two-factor sign-in is no longer required
